text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Full page report on Prime Minister Fatos Nano's visit to Italy where he will attend an international donors' conference expected to discuss how to rebuild Albania's shattered economy.
- Democratic Party denied that former president Sali Berisha is planning to set up committees in northern Albania to oust the Socialist-led ruling coalition.
- Some 5,000 Vlore residents have signed a petition asking for removal of former president Sali Berisha from the newly-elected parliament. Another 50,000 are expected to join the petition.
- The parliament passed a bill on Wednesday to audit the high-interest investment schemes and examine defunct pyramid schemes.
- Local lek currency opened firmer at about 150-157 against the dollar on Wednesday, compared with 165-170 last week.

- We will not reimburse people who lost their life savings deposited into collapsed pyramid investment scams, but we hope to compensate them by reviving our economy, Nano told reporters after meeting his Italian counterpart Romano Prodi.
- Prime Minister Fatos Nano's programme is a communist propaganda and will fail to help the country get out of crisis, Democratic Party secretary-general Genc Pollo said in a news conference.
- State-run television director Bardhyl Pollo said in a statement that parliament is not entitled by law to change the television board and its staff.
- Justice Minister arbitrarily ordered all Albanian courts to suspend the juridical processes for an unspecified period of time.

- Five parliamentary parties which make up the Union for Democracy coalition said they were concerned over the revenge policy of the Socialist Party which threatens the spirit of national reconciliation.

- International Monetary Fund (IMF) is fully committed to back the Albanian government in implementing its economic programme, the IMF representative in Tirana John King told Prime minister Fatos Nano.

- The paper warns Interior Minister Neritan Ceka not to dare to attack Shkoder residents under a pretext of fighting against criminal bands, saying Shkoder will remain a fiefdom of anti-communism in Albania.
